playbook:
When I hold K and I'm first to act or opponent checks, I bet to build value and apply pressure.

When I hold Q and I'm first to act, I default to checking unless the opponent's stack or prior behavior makes aggression necessary; if opponent checks to me, I bet to try to steal the pot.

When I hold Q and face a single-chip bet, I call—Q has enough showdown equity to contest small bets.

When I hold J and am first to act with a small or neutral stack situation, I check (pot control and avoid futile bluffs).

When I hold J and I'm behind in chips but not catastrophically short, I can open with a bet to apply pressure; when I am very short or already have a large deficit, avoid frequent bluffing with J (it tanked my results).

When the opponent bets after my check and I have Q or J and the bet is small relative to stacks, I call to see showdown; I fold only if the bet is large or I have strong reason to expect K.

When the opponent checks to me and I have a marginal hand (J or Q) but my stack position favors aggression, I bet to try to steal—otherwise check.

When in doubt about a single-chip decision with Q vs unknown, prefer calling over folding.

Always declare my actual card at showdown; never misdeclare.
